answer: The memory doesn't say what executes the code from the MCP `lua` tool. It only says that `lua` can do anything a user can script. On a server, MCP is off by default, and an admin turns it on in the APIs tab of the [[Dashboard]]. The memory doesn't describe a separate server feature that the `lua` tool depends on.

--- CHANGELOG.md ---
CHANGELOG | Edge > 2.10.0
* [[Dashboard]]: multi-space hosting with multiple accounts is here. A fresh install pointed at an empty folder opens a browser-based first-run **setup wizard** that creates an admin account and your first space, then serves it in place with no restart. One server can host any number of [[Space|spaces]], each bound to a URL prefix or hostname.
* [[Baked Sections]]: bake `${...}` Lua expressions and widgets into
  HTML-comment-delimited markdown (`<!--#lua EXPR -->` … `<!--/lua-->`).
* Space Lua: **code complete now shows documentation** (where available), all available via [[API/spacelua]] reflection APIs.
* Backend and CLI have been ported to Rust ([see background on this](https://no.silverbullet.plus/tech-stacks)), both should be behavior preserving (that is: you shouldn’t really notice):
  * The server backend (previously written in Go) has now been replaced by an adapted version of [SilverBullet+](https://silverbullet.plus/)’s backend written in Rust, more unifying those code bases.

--- MCP.md ---
Tools
SilverBullet can act as an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (Model Context Protocol) server, so AI assistants can read, write, query and pimp up your spaces.

MCP is available in [[Dashboard|multi-space mode]] and in [[Desktop]]. The endpoint is `/.mcp` on your server, for example `https://notes.example.com/.mcp`. A single-space server does not serve it. On a server it is off by default: an admin turns it on in the APIs tab of the [[Dashboard]].

--- CLI.md ---
Installation | Or pipe from stdin:
echo 'local x = 40; return x + 2' | sb lua

sb lua 'system.reboot()'       # after changing files outside sb (not needed after sb fs write/edit)
sb lua 'space.lint("Page")'    # problems on a page; space.lint() checks every page
```

To check a page without opening it in the editor, call [[API/space#space.lint]]: it runs the editor’s linters (frontmatter and data block YAML, `space-lua` syntax, objects checked against tag schemas, anchors) and renders every `${…}` directive and Lua code widget, returning a list of `{page, line, column, severity, message, source}` for the ones that fail. An empty list means no problems. A page written with `sb fs write` or `sb fs edit` (or through the [[MCP]]) has its scripts reloaded already, so `space.lint` sees them. Only after changing files by other means do you need `sb lua 'system.reboot()'` first.

--- MCP.md ---
Tools | Security
A connection carries the authority of the account that approved it, limited to the spaces chosen on the consent page. Page content read through MCP reaches the assistant (and its provider), and `lua` can do anything a user can script, so only connect assistants you trust with the spaces involved. Pages in shared spaces can be written by other people, and a page can contain text meant to steer the assistant, so be careful with spaces others can edit. Desktop's endpoint has no sign-in or consent page: while it is on, any program on your computer can use every registered space through it.

--- Workbench/Console.md ---
The log | The REPL
Type Lua at the bottom prompt and press Enter to run it. For a first experiment, enter `1 + 2`. The result is `3`. Console code can change your space when you call a write API, so use your own writable space for mutation examples.

The REPL can operate in two “contexts”:
* **Space context:** access to space-wide [[Space Lua]] variables and functions.
* **Page context:** also includes the current page’s variables and functions declared in [[Space Lua/Page Lua|page-lua blocks]].

What you can enter in the REPL:
* **Expressions** show their value: `1 + 2` shows `3`, and `"a", "b"` shows both values. A statement, like an assignment or a loop, shows nothing unless it ends with `return`.
* **Local variables:** a `local` you define stays available to later input, until you reload the page.
